statements.text: And now we’re faced with the possibility that artificial intelligence will make these problems worse. [...] As just one example, scammers can now use AI to clone a person’s voice to bypass voice authentication procedures.
statements.venue: Senate Banking Committee chairman statement on scams

statements.text: Artificial intelligence could cause even bigger changes in our financial system. We cannot sleepwalk into a major transformation of our economy, and put Americans’ money and financial futures at risk.
statements.venue: Opening statement, Senate Banking Committee hearing on AI in Financial Services

statements.text: AI is a tool, and we have the responsibility to set policies to ensure that when and if this tool is used, it’s used to make our economy work better for consumers and savers – not to exploit them.
statements.venue: Opening statement, Senate Banking Committee hearing on AI in Financial Services

statements.text: Consumers should expect, and Congress must require, rigorous testing and evaluation of AI models and programs before they are used in the real world, where they can cause real harm.
statements.venue: Opening statement, Senate Banking Committee hearing on AI in Financial Services

statements.text: I think one thing my colleagues and I can agree on is that the Silicon Valley ethos of move-fast-and-break-things is dangerous for both our financial system and our entire economy.
statements.venue: Opening statement, Senate Banking Committee hearing on AI in Financial Services

statements.text: I start with this, that I have a healthy skepticism of big corporations that come into Ohio and demand tax breaks and then override any local concerns and then try to raise our electric rates. I think you need reasonable regulation on any companies that come in, but you start with the fact that you need to be skeptical of these big companies that are buying their way into Ohio with low local income,

To me it's this, we need to make sure that there's local input on these locations of these, that they use union labor when they build them, that we don't use over-the-top tax breaks for these big tech companies and that people's electric bills, that people in Ohio shouldn't pay the electric bills for these out-of-state corporations,
Ohioans shouldn’t be forced to subsidize these costs and Ohioans — not Jon Husted and his billionaire friends — should get to decide if data centers are built in their community,
statements.venue: Statement to Ohio Capital Journal/Cleveland Scene

statements.text: Sure. AI is the next step, and there is no real consensus there. But to start with, you take away tax breaks, you require that the electricity costs are paid by the billionaires mostly from out of state, and you give local communities more say.
statements.venue: Pod Save interview posted on Sherrod Brown's Substack

statements.text: Did you know that one of the largest data centers in the world is being built right here in Wood County? [...] Why northwest Ohio? Because Jon Husted gave away $2.5 billion to these out of state corporations and billionaires.
